skill.name: setup
skill.description: Guide AI coding assistants through adding Shadcn UI components to this project.
skill.summary: Provides concise Shadcn UI component setup guidance.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the two prompt-only files. Manual review found concise Shadcn UI setup guidance and no prompt injection, credential handling, or data exfiltration intent.

content.value_statement: Adding UI components can be inconsistent when project setup guidance is scattered. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise Shadcn UI setup instructions.
actual_capabilities: Provides project-specific guidance for adding Shadcn UI components.
Documents the expected Shadcn component addition workflow.
Supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code in the same project context.
Keeps setup guidance short for quick assistant reference.
Includes a placeholder Shadcn component list for future expansion.
limitations: Only covers Shadcn UI setup guidance for this project.
Does not choose designs or build full features by itself.
May require package manager access and user approval before commands run.
The component list reference is currently empty.

use_cases.title: Add a UI Component
use_cases.description: Use the project setup note before adding a Shadcn UI component.

use_cases.title: Standardize Setup Guidance
use_cases.description: Give teammates a short reference for Shadcn component installation in this project.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Pairing
use_cases.description: Help an AI assistant follow the project-specific setup step before editing UI files.

prompt_templates.title: Add One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this setup skill to add a Shadcn UI button component. Confirm the component name before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the setup guidance for this project and explain how I should add a Shadcn UI component.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Component Addition
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the steps to add a Shadcn UI dialog component, including files you expect to change and checks to run.

prompt_templates.title: Update a Feature With Shadcn
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project setup guidance to add the best Shadcn UI components for a settings panel. Explain tradeoffs before editing.

output_examples.input: Add a Shadcn UI card component to support a dashboard summary.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the card component, follows the project setup guidance, and reports changed files and verification results.

output_examples.input: Explain how this project expects Shadcn UI components to be added.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes the setup note, identifies the component placeholder, and asks for the exact component name.

output_examples.input: Plan a settings panel using Shadcn UI components.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes suitable components, notes setup requirements, and separates installation steps from feature implementation.

best_practices: Confirm the exact Shadcn component name before applying setup guidance.
Review generated files after adding a component.
Keep component setup changes scoped to the current UI task.
anti_patterns: Running setup commands without user approval in restricted environments.
Adding Shadcn components that are not needed for the requested UI.
Mixing unrelated design refactors with component setup changes.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI assistants follow the project guidance for adding Shadcn UI components.

faq.question: Does it install components automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance that an assistant can follow with user approval.

faq.question: Can it be used with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It declares support for Codex, Claude, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include a full component catalog?
faq.answer: No. The component list file is present, but it is currently empty.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to one project?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is written for the source project that contains the skill.

faq.question: What should users review after using it?
faq.answer: Users should review generated component files, imports, styling changes, and any command output.
